SMTO-FIL-0010 — SMTO's file request had missing or conflicting details

GUID: 288c0188-b077-4dc3-a4a0-bd8d9f51ac03
Slug: file-invalid-invocation
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO asked to work with a file but left out a required detail or mixed options that can't be used together. The request was refused before it ran, so no files were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to try that file step again more simply, for example one file at a time, and name the exact file or folder. SMTO fills in these details itself, and a narrower request usually gives it one consistent set.
  2. Open Technical details in this panel and read which option was missing or conflicting. Mention it when you ask SMTO to try again. The message names the exact detail that was rejected, so SMTO can correct just that.
  3. If SMTO was reading a long file in parts, ask it to start reading that file again from the beginning. A damaged bookmark for continuing a read also causes this error, and a fresh read makes a new one.

What success looks like

  • The file step completes and the Task carries on without this message.

If it still fails

  • If the same step keeps failing, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to resend the identical request; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation was rejected before execution because its arguments failed the operation schema, carried a malformed continuation cursor, or combined mutually exclusive options (for example cursor with start_line, edit without new_text, diff with both or neither of other_path and text).

What this means

  • File arguments fail schema, cursor format/binding, required fields or mutually exclusive mode checks; edit/diff/list operations add their own contract checks. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • File arguments fail schema, cursor format/binding, required fields or mutually exclusive mode checks; edit/diff/list operations add their own contract checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the named operation and safe field-level rejection, including text-versus-byte and cursor-versus-offset options.

How to fix it

  • Read the receipt message for the rule that failed (gateway_core/file_contract.validate, file_read.read, file_mutate.edit/diff, file_walk.listing, CursorStore.read, or execution/work_preservation for malformed mutation structure). Resend the operation with arguments matching the advertised file.* schema, one consistent mode, and a cursor exactly as issued (fc1_ plus 24 URL-safe characters).
  • Correct the named fields and types against the advertised file operation schema.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended operation validates with one consistent set of fields.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
